title: Annual Report 2024 - Supervision and Regulation
summary: This section of the Federal Reserve's 2024 Annual Report provides a comprehensive inventory of supervised financial institutions as of year-end 2024, detailing the number and total assets of bank holding companies, state member banks, savings and loan holding companies, and financial market utilities under Fed oversight.
key_points: Federal Reserve supervised 3,747 U.S. bank holding companies (BHCs) controlling 95% of all insured commercial bank assets as of year-end 2024
8 Large Institution Supervision Coordinating Committee (LISCC) firms—U.S. G-SIBs—held $15.2 trillion in combined assets, representing the largest supervised portfolio by assets

The Federal Reserve categorized supervised institutions into five portfolios: Community Banking Organizations (3,408 firms, $3.0T assets), Regional Banking Organizations (105 firms, $3.0T), Large Banking Organizations (18 non-LISCC firms, $5.1T), Large FBOs (17 firms, $4.1T), and LISCC organizations
State member banks operated 47,434 branches representing 35% of all commercial banks and 70% of all commercial banking offices in the United States
497 domestic bank holding companies and 46 foreign banking organizations held Financial Holding Company (FHC) status as of year-end 2025
5 supervised insurance organizations (all SLHCs) held approximately $450 billion in total assets as of December 31, 2024
why_it_matters: This regulatory inventory establishes the foundational architecture of the U.S. banking system for reference purposes. The concentration of assets in 8 G-SIBs under LISCC supervision ($15.2T) and the bifurcation between community banks (3,408 institutions under $10B) versus larger institutions provides context for systemic risk distribution. However, this is static institutional data, not actionable market structure intelligence.
market_structure_context: The report describes the supervisory architecture of the U.S. banking system, noting Federal Reserve oversight of financial market utilities (FMUs) designated as systemically important by FSOC in July 2012. However, it contains no information on trading market structure, order routing, clearing mechanisms, or market operations.
